{
  "root_cause": "The NAT access list 'NAT-ACL' uses an overly broad 'permit ip any any' statement instead of specifying only external/internet-bound subnets, causing the router to inappropriately perform NAT on traffic between internal servers on different VLANs.",
  "confidence": 95,
  "evidence": "show ip nat translations shows an active TCP translation between internal private IP addresses (10.10.5.5 and 10.10.20.10), and show access-lists NAT-ACL confirms rule 10 is 'permit ip any any' with over 4000 matches.",
  "next_command": "show running-config | include ip nat",
  "fix_steps": [
    "Enter global configuration mode on the router.",
    "Modify the NAT access list (NAT-ACL) to specifically permit only internal source subnets and deny internal-to-internal traffic, or restrict the permit statement to target external destinations.",
    "Clear existing NAT translations using 'clear ip nat translation *'.",
    "Verify that communication between the two internal servers no longer shows up in NAT translations and that the application functions correctly."
  ]
}

parsed.root_cause: The NAT access list 'NAT-ACL' uses an overly broad 'permit ip any any' statement instead of specifying only external/internet-bound subnets, causing the router to inappropriately perform NAT on traffic between internal servers on different VLANs.
parsed.evidence: show ip nat translations shows an active TCP translation between internal private IP addresses (10.10.5.5 and 10.10.20.10), and show access-lists NAT-ACL confirms rule 10 is 'permit ip any any' with over 4000 matches.
fix_steps: Enter global configuration mode on the router.
Modify the NAT access list (NAT-ACL) to specifically permit only internal source subnets and deny internal-to-internal traffic, or restrict the permit statement to target external destinations.
Clear existing NAT translations using 'clear ip nat translation *'.
Verify that communication between the two internal servers no longer shows up in NAT translations and that the application functions correctly.
